subject: Pilot connection limits & ratecard — post-call recap
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Ana Rodrigues <ana@cloudpay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot connection limits & ratecard — post-call recap

Hi Ana / Mike,

Thanks again for taking the time today — quick recap and proposed next steps from Redwood on the performance / SLO side so we can size the pilot correctly.

Highlights from our discussion (please confirm):
- Primary workload: payroll submission + near-real-time status updates.
- Target p95 latency: 200ms for generation endpoints (text-only).
- Steady-state concurrent active requests (parallel requests): ~300.
- Peak bursts during payroll cutoff: up to ~1,200 concurrent active requests for ~1–3 minutes.
- Persistent streaming sessions: ~80–100 concurrent streams for live status events (server-sent events / websockets).
- Connection pooling preference: long-lived TLS sockets reused (client library will keep ~200 sockets open across 12 regions).

Questions / open items for CloudPay to confirm:
1) Is the 1,200 concurrent burst a single-region event or distributed across regions?
2) Do you expect many long-polling idle connections (i.e., many sockets but low request rate per socket) or dense active requests per socket?
3) Which endpoints will see the highest concurrency (submit-payments vs status-read)?

Our suggested pilot ask from Redwood (pending your confirmation):
- Pilot parallel request quota: 400 concurrent active requests (with burst allowance to 1,200 for 3 minutes).
- Connection pool sockets: 250 reserved persistent connections.
- Streaming session quota: 120 concurrent streams.
- Observability: token-level metrics + per-route latency traces enabled; we will provide a sample dashboard.

Next steps we propose:
- CloudPay to confirm the three open items above by Tue 5/17.
- Redwood to share draft ratecard + M.A.P and a connection-pool diagram by end of day Wed 5/18.
- Engineering onboarding call (30m) week of May 24 to walk pilot traffic routing and auth.

Attaching a short pilot checklist and a template mutual-action-plan in the follow-up from our side.

Thanks —
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: mutual-action-plan.xlsx]
From: Ana Rodrigues <ana@cloudpay.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Mike Sanders <mike@cloudpay.com>
Date: 2027-05-13T08:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot connection limits & ratecard — post-call recap

Thanks Jasmine — quick answers inline and a couple clarifications.

On 2027-05-12 Jasmine Liu wrote:
> Highlights from our discussion (please confirm):
> - Primary workload: payroll submission + near-real-time status updates.
> - Target p95 latency: 200ms for generation endpoints (text-only).
> - Steady-state concurrent active requests (parallel requests): ~300.
> - Peak bursts during payroll cutoff: up to ~1,200 concurrent active requests for ~1–3 minutes.
> - Persistent streaming sessions: ~80–100 concurrent streams for live status events (server-sent events / websockets).
> - Connection pooling preference: long-lived TLS sockets reused (client library will keep ~200 sockets open across 12 regions).

Confirmations / clarifications:
- The 1,200 burst is primarily US-east and US-west (about 70/30 split). We also have smaller regional peaks in EU during our payroll windows.
- We will have many long-polling connections in addition to active requests; roughly 2.5x sockets to active requests during steady-state. Expect socket-heavy behavior.
- Highest concurrency will be on submit-payments endpoints — the status-read traffic is much lighter per socket.

Two questions on Redwood rate limiting model:
1) Can Redwood apply a token-bucket style burst window per-project (we prefer a short burst window vs strict per-second cap)?
2) How are streaming sessions counted against concurrency quotas — per open websocket or per active stream event?

Attached a small sample traffic extract to help sizing (sample_traffic.csv).

We can confirm the items by 5/17 but would appreciate Redwood offering pilot numbers based on the socket-heavy profile.

Best,
Ana Rodrigues
Head of Integrations, CloudPay
[Attachment: sample_traffic.csv]
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Ana Rodrigues <ana@cloudpay.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-18T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot connection limits & ratecard — post-call recap

Hi Ana — thanks for the quick turnaround and the sample traffic. Based on the socket-heavy profile you described, we adjusted the pilot proposal below.

Proposal (pilot, 30 days):
- Parallel active requests (concurrent): 400 reserved, with burst allowance up to 1,200 for 3 minutes (token-bucket style burst window configurable).
- Connection pool: 300 reserved persistent TLS sockets (we increased from 250 to provide headroom given your 2.5x socket ratio).
- Streaming sessions: 130 concurrent streams counted per open websocket (each open connection that carries an active stream counts as 1).
- Rate model: per-project token bucket + per-route safeguards. Bursts are allowed up to the configured token-bucket depth; sustained over-limit will trigger soft-429 with graceful fallback to reduced-quality model.
- Latency SLO: target p95 = 250ms for the pilot (we will tune kernel selection and batching profiles to move towards 200ms once in production).

Attached: redwood-ratecard-v1.pdf (pilot pricing), connpool-diagram.png (how sockets map to worker pools), mutual-action-plan.xlsx (MAP draft).

Engineer notes / operational hooks:
- We will provision a trial API key scoped to your project and enable debug metrics (per-token, per-route, per-model) for the pilot.
- We recommend using our SDK to get automatic connection reuse and keepalive; manual pooling is supported if you run a custom client.
- If you want strict per-second RPS caps on particular endpoints (e.g., submit-payments), we can configure per-route rate limits in addition to the global token bucket.

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached MAP and redwood-ratecard-v1.pdf and share any commercial redlines by 5/21.
2) If MAP is acceptable, sign and return — we will issue the pilot key and schedule the 30m onboarding call (preferred slots: 5/20 10am PT or 5/21 2pm PT).
3) Engineering onboarding will validate telemetry and run a short synthetic ramp to validate burst behavior.

Let us know which slot works and any commercial constraints. Happy to jump on a quick call if you prefer to walk through the diagram.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
[Attachments: redwood-ratecard-v1.pdf, connpool-diagram.png, mutual-action-plan.xlsx]
